newsitem.title: FRANCE: Kohl says central bank independence preferable.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says central bank independence preferable.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl told French television that the experience of Germany and other countries showed that it was preferable for central banks to be independent.

Asked in an interview on TF1 television to comment on the debate over whether some sort of European economic government was needed alongside or above the European Central Bank, Kohl said, "I find this debate totally unnecessary. We have had an independent Bundesbank for many years, and it is really independent. It hasn't done the Germans, nor the deutschemark, any harm and we will now have a European central bank.

"But this central bank isn't on the moon, it is in the middle of Europe and those who sit on it know the realities of Europe such as the job market, economic development and inflation rates. Why should that not work?
"I don't have this mistrust, not at all," he said.
A transcript of the interview, scheduled to be broadcast at 1800 GMT on Sunday, was sent to Reuters.

"Naturally I admit that it is sometimes very useful for a government to push the bank in a certain direction. But on the other hand, I say just as clearly that my experience, the experience not just of Germany, shows that it quite good if the government cannot manipulate (the bank)," Kohl said.
He said there was no cause for concern.
"I am personally quite convinced that 10 years after the euro and the European central bank are introduced, most people in Paris will say: 'It was a good decision'," he said.
